prOriginalConhecido.nota: calcom/cal.com now redirects to calcom/cal.diy (renamed). PR #22532 head sha equals benchmark head 5fd11f9f; squash commit cb786923. Its tree differs from the head only by unrelated main changes (apps/web version bump, one unrelated locale key).

tps.bug: connectedCalendarsHandler instantiates CalendarCacheRepository directly instead of the feature-flag-aware factory, so cache status is queried and shown even when calendar-cache is disabled.
tps.evidenciaOpus: connectedCalendars.handler.ts:28 does `new CalendarCacheRepository()` instead of going through CalendarCache.init (calendar-cache.ts:22-29), bypassing the feature-flag check and leaving the PR's own CalendarCacheRepositoryMock.getCacheStatusByCredentialIds dead. Effect is an extra groupBy and possibly showing stale cache timestamps while the cache is disabled.
tps.evidenciaAstra: connectedCalendars.handler.ts:28-29 directly constructs the repository, whose calendar-cache.repository.ts:173-182 unconditionally queries Prisma. This bypasses calendar-cache.ts:24-28 and the disabled implementation returning [] in calendar-cache.repository.mock.ts:27-29, allowing cache status and actions to remain visible while caching is disabled (CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:69-107).

tps.bug: The dev script writes tunnelmole output to a fixed /tmp/tmole.log, so a local attacker's symlink at that path could make it overwrite an arbitrary file.
tps.evidenciaOpus: scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh:4,35-36 does `rm -f /tmp/tmole.log` before redirecting, which removes a pre-planted symlink; exploiting it needs a local attacker winning a race on a developer machine for a local dev helper script, so there is no practical problem to report.
tps.evidenciaAstra: scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh:4 uses a predictable shared temporary path, and lines 34-35 perform an unchecked removal followed by a symlink-following truncating redirect. Although successful removal unlinks an existing symlink, an attacker-owned link can survive a denied removal in sticky /tmp, or be inserted between removal and opening; on systems permitting symlink following, the victim's writable target is truncated.
